Mordred: Character in Arthurian legend. Mordred or Modred ( or; Welsh: Medraut or Medrawt) is a major figure in the legend of King Arthur.
The most prosperous king of Ayutthaya's Prasat Thong dynasty handed extraordinary power to a Greek adventurer named Constantine Phaulkon. Which Thai monarch was he?
Narai: 27th monarch of the Ayutthaya Kingdom (1656–1688)
Shared across Jainism, Hinduism, Buddhism, and Sikhism, this state of liberation marks the end of the cycle of rebirth and the extinguishing of worldly passions — what is it?
Nirvana: Liberation from repeated rebirth in saṃsāra.
Four days after D-Day, a Waffen-SS company destroyed this French village and killed 642 civilians in retaliation for Resistance activity, including the death of a captured SS officer — which village?
Oradour-sur-Glane massacre: 1944 mass killing by Nazi German soldiers in France.
This senior Soviet intelligence officer orchestrated Leon Trotsky's assassination in Mexico in 1940 and later ran spy operations targeting the Manhattan Project — who was he?
A protégé of the dictator Sulla, this Roman general and statesman celebrated three triumphs and was elected consul on three separate occasions during the late Republic — who was he?
Pompey: Roman general and statesman (106–48 BC)
R. Budd Dwyer: American politician (1939–1987). Dwyer committed suicide by gunshot during a press conference following his conviction for accepting a bribe in the CTA scandal.
The daughter of actors Pushpavalli and Gemini Ganesan, this Hindi-film actress starred in more than 200 films and received India's Padma Shri in 2010 — who is she?
Nicknamed 'the Mad Baron,' this Baltic German warlord tried to revive the Mongol Empire under the Bogd Khan and expelled Chinese troops from Mongolia in 1921 — who was he?
Roman von Ungern-Sternberg: Russian general and warlord (1886–1921)

The only person ever elected governor of two different US states, he also served as president of the Republic of Texas after spending years living with the Cherokee, who nicknamed him 'Raven' — who was he?
Sam Houston: American general and statesman (1793–1863)
Known as 'the eye of Ra,' this Egyptian warrior goddess of medicine is often linked with Hathor and Bastet — who is she?
Sekhmet: Ancient Egyptian goddess. Sekhmet is also a solar deity, sometimes given the epithet "the eye of Ra".
Born in Singapore in 1983, this former Xiaomi finance chief has run a wildly popular ByteDance-owned video app since 2021 — who is he?
Shou Zi Chew: Singaporean business executive (born 1983)
A barrister who founded his own Democratic Party, this politician stepped up after Makarios III's death to lead his Mediterranean island nation as president from 1977 to 1988 — who was he?
Spyros Kyprianou: President of Cyprus from 1977 to 1988.

Serving as Turkey's Interior Minister from 2016 to 2023 after the surprise resignation of his predecessor, this deputy chairman of the Justice and Development Party was known for accusing opposition figures of siding with terrorists — who is he?
One of the fifty Nereids and daughter of the sea god Nereus, this Greek sea nymph appears in the Trojan War cycle of myth — who is she?
A legendary tenth-year siege in Greek mythology, sparked when Paris took Helen from her husband—immortalized in Homer's Iliad and Odyssey—what's this ancient conflict?
Trojan War: Legendary war in Greek mythology. The Trojan War was a legendary conflict in Greek mythology that took place around the thirteenth century or early twelfth century BC.
The last man standing in the Year of the Four Emperors, this Roman founded the Flavian dynasty and was the first emperor to rise from an equestrian family. Who was he?
Vespasian: Roman emperor from AD 69 to 79.
Generally marked by widespread violence and destruction, this armed conflict between states or organized groups is typically waged in pursuit of political, economic, or territorial aims — what is it?
War: Intense armed conflict. It is generally characterized by widespread violence, destruction, and mortality, using regular or irregular military forces.

An explorer, lawyer and one of colonial New South Wales' wealthiest figures, he co-founded Australia's first independent newspaper and championed emancipists, trial by jury and self-government — who was he?
William Wentworth: Australian statesman, writer and explorer.
The only Israeli soldier killed during a daring 1976 hostage-rescue raid on a hijacked airliner in Uganda, he was the elder brother of a future Israeli prime minister — who was he?
Which of these people was born first?
Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Ma Jun (mechanical engineer) (born 200) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Jīvaka (born 401 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the astronomer from these four.
Giordano Bruno is an astronomer. Bruno's pantheism was not taken lightly by the church, nor was his teaching of metempsychosis regarding the reincarnation of the soul.
Which of these is a mathematician?
Roger Penrose is a mathematician. Sir Roger Penrose (born 8 August 1931) is an English mathematician, mathematical physicist, and philosopher of science.
What is the atomic number of Cadmium?
Cadmium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cd and atomic number 48.
What is the atomic number of Lead?
Lead is a chemical element with the symbol Pb (from the Latin plumbum) and atomic number 82.
In what year was John von Neumann born?
John von Neumann: During World War II, von Neumann worked on the Manhattan Project.
In what year was Manmohan Singh born?
Manmohan Singh: A member of the Indian National Congress, Singh was the first and remains the only Sikh prime minister of India.
In what year was Paracelsus born?
Paracelsus also had a substantial influence as a prophet or diviner, his "Prognostications" being studied by Rosicrucians in the 17th century.
In what year did B. R. Ambedkar die?
B. R. Ambedkar: Ambedkar served as Law and Justice minister in the first cabinet of Jawaharlal Nehru.
In what year did Tomitaro Makino die?
Tomitaro Makino (牧野 富太郎, Makino Tomitarō; 24 April 1862 – 18 January 1957) was a pioneer Japanese botanist noted for his taxonomic work.
In what year was Pluto discovered?
Pluto (minor-planet number 134340) is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
TypeScript: Anders Hejlsberg. TypeScript (TS) is a high-level programming language that adds static typing with optional type annotations to JavaScript.
Pethidine: Pfizer. Pethidine, also known as meperidine and sold under the brand name Demerol among others, is a fully synthetic opioid pain medication of the phenylpiperidine class.
In which country is Kazan phenomenon?
Kazan phenomenon: Soviet Union. The Kazan mafia was known to be particularly cruel in their extortion tactics, and periodically brought in reinforcements from Tatarstan.
Who is credited with discovering Seaborgium?
Seaborgium: Yuri Oganessian. Seaborgium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Sg and atomic number 106.
Who is credited with discovering Hydrogen cyanide?
Hydrogen cyanide: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Hydrogen cyanide (also called prussic acid) is a chemical compound with the formula HCN and structural formula H−C≡N.
Who is credited with discovering Tungsten?
Tungsten: Juan José Elhuyar. Tungsten (also called wolfram) is a chemical element; it has symbol W (from German: Wolfram) and atomic number 74.
This tsetse-fly-borne parasitic infection, caused by a protozoan, disproportionately affects humans and cattle across Africa — what is it?
Atrocities in the Congo Free State

African trypanosomiasis is an insect-borne parasitic infection of humans and other animals caused by the protozoan species Trypanosoma brucei, which is transmitted by the bite of an infected tsetse fly.
Named after a French physicist considered a father of electromagnetism, this SI unit measures electric current as one coulomb of charge passing a point per second. What unit is it?
Ampere (symbol: A), often shortened to amp, is the unit of electric current in the International System of Units (SI).
Marked by right lower abdominal pain, nausea, and fever, this common inflammatory condition is typically caused by a blockage from a small hard mass called a fecalith — name the condition?
Appendicitis is inflammation of the appendix.
Found throughout North America from Canada to northern Mexico, this sea eagle has two subspecies and forms a pair with the white-tailed eagle—name it.
Bald eagle (Haliaeetus leucocephalus) is a bird of prey found in North America.
Present in every living cell and abundant in liver and meats, this B vitamin acts as an enzyme cofactor and takes its name from the Greek for 'life' — what is it?
Biotin (also known as vitamin B7 and vitamin H) is one of the B vitamins - a group of essential dietary micronutrients.
This American actor played Kyle Parks on Lifetime's The Client List before joining the cast of Revenge as Ben Hunter — who is he?
Brian Hallisay (born October 31, 1978) is an American actor, known for his roles as Will Davis in The CW drama series Privileged and Kyle Parks in the Lifetime drama series The Client List.
Nine to ten times as massive as the Sun and expanded to 71 times its radius, this blue-loop giant in the constellation Carina ranks second only to Sirius in night-sky brightness — which star?
Canopus is the brightest star in the southern constellation of Carina and the second-brightest star in the night sky.
Built under license from the Soviet MiG-21, this Chinese fighter jet carries the NATO reporting name Fishcan and specializes in short-range air combat — what aircraft is it?
Chengdu J-7 (pinyin: Jin-7; third generation export version J-7; NATO reporting name: Fishcan) is a Chinese fighter aircraft.
A scale insect native to tropical and subtropical parts of the Americas that lives on prickly-pear cacti, this parasite is the source of the natural dye carmine — which insect?
Cochineal (-eel, US also, -eel; Dactylopius coccus) is a scale insect in the suborder Sternorrhyncha, from which the natural dye carmine is derived.

Though Colin Maclaurin published special cases two years earlier, this determinant-based method for solving linear systems bears the name of the mathematician who generalized it in 1750 — what's it known as?
Cramer's rule is an explicit formula for the solution of a system of linear equations with as many equations as unknowns, valid whenever the system has a unique solution.
Caused by either too little insulin or cells that ignore it, this condition keeps blood sugar stubbornly high and comes chiefly in a type 1 and a type 2 — what is it?
Diabetes is a group of common endocrine diseases characterized by sustained high blood sugar levels.
Which natural science examines how living things relate to their environment, spanning the individual, population, community, ecosystem, and biosphere levels?
Ecology (from Ancient Greek (okos) 'house' and - (-loga) 'study of') is the natural science of the relationships among living organisms and their environment.

Discovered in January 2005 by a Palomar Observatory team and named after a Greco-Roman goddess of strife, this trans-Neptunian object is the most massive known dwarf planet in the solar system — which one?
Eris (dwarf planet) (minor-planet number 136199) is the most massive and second-largest known dwarf planet in the Solar System.
This field of study, related to economics and business administration, is typically divided into personal, corporate, and public branches. What field is it?
Finance refers to monetary resources as well as the discipline that studies such resources, with related concepts such as money, currency, assets and liabilities.
This scholarly discipline covers the link between food and culture, from recipes and regional cooking styles to the rigorous science of good eating — what's it called?

Gastronomy is the study of the relationship between food and culture, the art of preparing and serving rich or delicate and appetizing food, the cooking styles of particular regions, and the science of good eating.
A friar, mathematician, and meteorologist who quietly worked out the laws of heredity with garden peas — and only got credit long after his death — who was this founder of genetics?
Gregor Mendel (20 July 1822 - 6 January 1884) was an Austrian biologist, meteorologist, mathematician, Augustinian friar and abbot of St.
This discipline governs the design and formal description ('blazon') of coats of arms, crests, and other armorial bearings — what is it called?
Heraldry (also known as armoury) is a discipline relating to the design, display, study and transmission of armorial bearings.

This altered mental state involves intensely focused attention, reduced awareness of surroundings, and heightened responsiveness to suggestion, though scientists still debate whether it's truly a distinct state of consciousness — what is it?

Hypnosis is a human condition involving focused attention (the selective attention/selective inattention hypothesis, SASI), reduced peripheral awareness, and an enhanced capacity to respond to suggestion.

In 1897, this British physicist showed that cathode rays were made of previously unknown negatively charged particles far smaller than atoms — the first subatomic particle ever identified. Who was he?
J. J. Thomson (18 December 1856 - 30 August 1940) was a British physicist.

After leaving the company where he led industrial design for decades, this British-American designer founded the creative collective LoveFrom, which now works with Ferrari, Airbnb, and OpenAI. Who is he?
Jony Ive (born 27 February 1967) is a British-American designer.
Originally a water-retrieving gun dog from Italy's Po Delta marshes, this breed later became prized for hunting truffles once its wetland habitat was drained — what breed is it?
Lagotto Romagnolo is an Italian breed of dog.

The second woman to earn a physics doctorate from the University of Vienna, this Austrian-Swedish scientist became the first female full physics professor in Germany — and was instrumental in discovering nuclear fission. Who is she?
Lise Meitner (7 November 1878 - 27 October 1968) was an Austrian and Swedish nuclear physicist who was instrumental in the discovery of nuclear fission.

Made by every living organism and responsible for much of the sour taste in fruit, this dicarboxylic food additive's salt form also serves as a key intermediate in the cell's central metabolic energy cycle — what compound is it?
Malic acid is an organic compound with the molecular formula HO2CCH(OH)CH2CO2H.
A waxy crystalline compound from peppermint and corn mint, it triggers a cooling sensation and works as a mild local anesthetic to soothe a sore throat — what is it?
Menthol is a monoterpenoid organic compound that occurs naturally in the oils of certain plants in the mint family, such as corn mint and peppermint.

Native to Africa, Asia, and Oceania, with one invasive species now in the southern U.S., this reptile genus ranges from 20 centimeters long to over 3 meters in the Komodo dragon — name this group of lizards?
Monitor lizard are lizards in the genus Varanus, the only extant genus in the family Varanidae.

Sometimes reaching two meters long but often thinner than a millimeter or two wide, these thread-like parasitoid worms turn up in damp puddles, troughs, and swimming pools as adults — what phylum is this?

Nematomorpha (sometimes called Gordiacea, and commonly known as horsehair worms, hairsnakes, or Gordian worms) are a phylum of parasitoid animals similar to yet distinct from nematode worms in morphology, hence the name.
Many species in this bird family scavenge alongside pigeons and gulls, while two of its city-dwelling members are famous for nesting directly on buildings — which family are they?
Old World sparrow are groups of small passerine birds forming the family Passeridae.
Making up the order Psittaciformes, these birds are known for a strong curved beak, upright stance, and clawed feet, with a third of all species threatened by extinction — name the group?
Parrot (order Psittaciformes), also known as psittacines from the name of the type genus Psittacus, are birds with a strong curved beak, upright stance, and clawed feet.
Made in the body from the amino acid L-phenylalanine, this natural stimulant also turns up in fermented chocolate and inhibits a transporter called VMAT2 — what is it?
Phenethylamine (PEA) is an organic compound, natural monoamine alkaloid, and trace amine, which acts as a central nervous system stimulant in humans.
It looks like a single point of light, but this brightest star of Ursa Minor is actually a triple star system parked near the north celestial pole — what is it?
Polaris is a yellow supergiant star in the northern circumpolar constellation of Ursa Minor.

This sympathomimetic medication is best known as a nasal decongestant, though at higher doses it can act as a stimulant and appetite suppressant, making it a common drug of abuse — what's the compound called?
Pseudoephedrine is a sympathomimetic medication which is used as a nasal decongestant to treat nasal congestion.
With roughly 12,000 living species split across four classic orders — including the single-species tuatara branch — what ectothermic class is this?
Reptile are tetrapod vertebrate animals with an ectothermic metabolism and amniotic development.

Known from complete specimens found in Bolivia, this extinct armored jawless fish from the Ordovician period resembled a slender tadpole with eyes set like car headlamps on its oversized head — what is it?
Sacabambaspis is an extinct genus of armored jawless fish which lived in the Ordovician period.
Applied practically by Archimedes for the quadrature of a parabola, what do we call the addition of infinitely many terms, one after another, central to calculus?
Series (mathematics) is, roughly speaking, an addition of infinitely many terms, one after the other.
Which genus of about 28 grass species includes one member grown worldwide both as a cereal grain for human consumption and as fodder for livestock?
Sorghum (genus) is a genus of about 28 species of flowering plants in the grass family (Poaceae).
A single-seat, twin-engine, supermaneuverable 4.5-generation fighter derived from the Su-27, it was relabeled from "Su-27M" after the Soviet collapse to court export buyers — which Russian jet?
Sukhoi Su-35 (NATO reporting name: Flanker-E/M, occasionally nicknamed "Super Flanker") is the designation for two improved derivatives of the Su-27 air superiority fighter.
This group of inherited blood disorders reduces the body's hemoglobin production, sometimes causing anemia, an enlarged spleen, and stunted growth in children — what condition is it?
Thalassemia are a group of inherited blood disorders that manifest as the production of reduced hemoglobin.

This androgenic anabolic steroid, part of the nandrolone group, is marketed in ester forms for veterinary use — commonly given to livestock to boost muscle growth and appetite — what's the steroid called?
Trenbolone is an androgen and anabolic steroid (AAS) of the nandrolone group which itself was never marketed for human use.

This flowering plant genus, the largest in its family with over 680 species, is found mostly across the temperate Northern Hemisphere but also as far-flung as Hawaii and the Andes. What is this plant commonly called?
Viola (plant) is a genus of flowering plants in the family Violaceae.
Common across Europe and also found in Asia, this large carpenter bee bores its nest into dead wood rather than building a hive — which species?
Xylocopa violacea is the common European species of carpenter bee, and one of the largest bees in Europe.
Taken by mouth, smeared as a cream, or injected, this antiviral medication is a frontline treatment for herpes simplex, chickenpox, and shingles. What is it?
Aciclovir: Antiviral medication used against herpes, chickenpox, and shingles.
A broad-spectrum benzimidazole drug, it clears out an alarming roll call of intestinal parasites — pinworm, hookworm, ascariasis, giardiasis and more. Which medication is it?
The heaviest member of its family, this Southeastern U.S. reptile sees males stretch up to 15 feet and tip 1,000 pounds — and it's the larger of just two surviving species in its genus. What is it?
American alligator: Crocodilian native to the Southeastern United States.
Known in veterinary medicine as inappetence when it strikes cats, dogs, or cattle, which general medical term describes any loss of appetite — a symptom rather than a diagnosis in itself?
Anorexia (symptom): Loss of appetite. The symptom also occurs in non-human animals, such as cats, dogs, cattle, goats, and sheep.

Nicknamed for its resemblance to a stinging insect, this orb-weaver spider sports bold yellow, white, and black bands across Central and Northern Europe, parts of Asia and Africa, and even the Azores — what species is it?
Argiope bruennichi: Species of orb-weaver spider. Like many other members of the same genus Argiope, this species has distinctive yellow, white and black markings on its abdomen.
This broad category of technology uses machines and predetermined rules to reduce the need for human intervention in factories, boilers, and telephone switching — what is it?
Automation: Use of various control systems for operating equipment.
Sharing its engine, transmission, and rotor system with the Huey utility helicopter, this rapidly-developed attack chopper became America's dedicated gunship escort in the Vietnam War — what is it?
Bell AH-1 Cobra: Family of attack helicopters.
This organ stores urine received from the kidneys via the ureters before it exits through the urethra, and gives us the medical term 'cystitis' when inflamed — what is it?
Bladder: Organ in vertebrates that collects and stores urine from the kidneys before disposal.
Named from Greek words for 'slow' and 'heart,' this condition means a resting heart rate under 60 beats per minute — sometimes normal in well-conditioned athletes — which condition?
Bradycardia: Heart rate below the normal range.
Common in cancer, heart failure, and other serious illnesses, this syndrome causes muscle wasting that better nutrition alone can't reverse — what is it?
In 1886 this German engineer patented what's considered the first practical automobile, and his Mannheim company later merged with Daimler — who is he?
Carl Benz: German designer and engineer (1844–1929)
Documented anatomically since the time of Hippocrates over 2,000 years ago, this roughly 4-centimeter-long fibromuscular organ connects the vagina to the uterine cavity. What structure is this?
Cervix: Lower part of the uterus in the female reproductive system.
This complex of DNA and histone proteins packages long strands of genetic material into compact structures while controlling access for transcription, replication and repair — what is it?
Chromatin: Complex of DNA and protein in eukaryotic cells.
This genus of demersal fish, named by Linnaeus in 1758, includes an Atlantic and a Pacific species prized for their mild flavor and flaky white flesh — what fish is it?
Cod: Common name for several fish, but mainly the demersal genus Gadus.
With a long hooked bill and webbing between all four toes, this fish-eating aquatic bird family includes the 'great' species commonly seen around Britain and Ireland — what are they called?
Cormorant: Family of aquatic birds. The common names "cormorant" and "shag" have been assigned to different species in the family somewhat haphazardly.
Sometimes called 'bipolar III,' this mood disorder involves cycling periods of mild depression and elevated mood that never reach the severity of full manic or depressive episodes — what is it?
Cyclothymia: Mental disorder. Cyclothymia differs from bipolar disorder in the fact that major depression and mania are not found.
Whether for an object, a process, or a system, this is the intentional concept or proposal created by a thinking agent, balancing purpose, aesthetics, and constraints — what single word names it?
Design: Plan for the construction of an object or system.
Brought to Australia as an infant, this geologist joined Shackleton's Nimrod Expedition and became a leading figure of the Heroic Age of Antarctic exploration — who is it?
Douglas Mawson: Australian geologist and explorer of the Antarctic (1882–1958)
This membrane-bound series of protein complexes shuttles electrons through redox reactions, building a proton gradient that ultimately powers the synthesis of ATP — what's it called?
Electron transport chain: Energy-producing metabolic pathway.
Named from the Greek for 'red skin,' this bacterial infection produces a raised, sharply defined, bright-red rash typically on the face or legs — what's the condition?
Erysipelas: Human disease from a bacterial infection of the skin.
Also nicknamed the 'baum' or 'sweet' variety, this mustelid species ranges across much of the continent into Asia Minor, the Caucasus, and parts of Iran, Iraq, and Syria. What animal is it?
European pine marten: Species of mammal in the mustelid family.

These small to medium passerine birds have stout conical bills for cracking seeds and nuts, a worldwide native range excluding Australia and the poles, and include canaries, siskins, and Darwin's famous Galápagos group — what bird family is this?
Finch: Family of birds. The true finches are small to medium-sized passerine birds in the family Fringillidae.
This Austrian economist shared the 1974 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences with Gunnar Myrdal for his work on how prices communicate information — who is he?
Friedrich Hayek: Austrian economist and philosopher (1899–1992)

Working at Tuskegee Institute, this agricultural scientist urged cotton farmers to plant peanuts and sweet potatoes instead, publishing dozens of practical bulletins to fight soil depletion. Who is he?
George Washington Carver: American botanist and inventor (1864–1943)
This term describes the overall system of rules, processes, and power structures that steers decision-making within an organized group — what is it?
Governance: Processes of interacting with people and making decisions.
Occurring in any of the senses, this perception feels completely real despite the absence of any actual external stimulus — what is it?
Hallucination: Perception that only seems real.
With over 800 species lugging borrowed snail shells to shield their soft, non-calcified abdomens, this crustacean is essentially homeless without a hand-me-down home. What is it?
Stretching about a meter from crown to tail-tip, this deep-blue South American parrot is the largest of its kind and can be mistaken for a smaller relative — which vulnerable parrot?
Co-creator of the AlexNet neural network and former chief scientist at OpenAI, this computer scientist has won NeurIPS's Test of Time Award three years running — who is he?

This Mexican neurophysiologist studied shamanism, meditation, and telepathy through the scientific method, wrote more than 50 books on the subjects, and then vanished without a trace in December 1994 — who was he?
Jacobo Grinberg: Mexican pseudoscientist, neurophysiologist and psychologist.
This English mathematician dreamed up the cellular automaton known as the Game of Life and spent his later years at Princeton — who was he?
Also called Bushman's tea, the leaves of this East African shrub are chewed as a recreational stimulant, most popular among Somalis and Yemenis — what is it?
The last member of the actinide series, this synthetic element honors the man who invented the cyclotron — the very machine used to discover so many artificial elements. Which element is it?
Lawrencium: Chemical element with atomic number 103 (Lr)
Named in honor of a pioneer of sterile surgery, this genus of bacteria causes a rare but serious foodborne illness with a fatality rate up to 30 percent — what is it?
Listeria: Genus of bacteria. Listeria is a genus of bacteria that acts as an intracellular parasite in mammals.
Named from a Greek root meaning 'light' or 'brightness' in reference to its luminous, reflective eyes, this genus includes the bobcat among its four wild cat species — which genus?
Lynx: Genus of medium-sized wild cats.
A Russian pediatric endocrinologist also known by the surname Faassen, this woman is the elder child of Russia's president. Who is she?
Maria Vorontsova: Daughter of Vladimir Putin (born 1985)
This waxy crystalline compound from peppermint and corn mint produces a cooling sensation when inhaled or rubbed on skin, and brings local-anesthetic relief to a sore throat — what is it?
Menthol: Organic compound used as flavouring and analgesic.

Given the NATO reporting name 'Hip,' this Soviet-designed helicopter family has been in continuous production since 1975 as a medium twin-turbine transport, with an armed gunship variant — which aircraft?
Mil Mi-17: Family of Russian military transport helicopters.
Built with a slender segmented body and a long piercing-and-sucking proboscis, this family of 3,600 fly species diversified back in the Cretaceous — what are they?
Mosquito: Family of flies. The word mosquito (formed by mosca and diminutive -ito) is Spanish and Portuguese for little fly.

This branch of alternative medicine rests on vitalism and folk healing rather than evidence, and its grab-bag of 'natural' methods runs from the thoroughly discredited to certain accepted psychotherapies. What is it?
Naturopathy: Form of alternative medicine. The ethics of naturopathy have been called into question by medical professionals and its practice has been characterized as quackery.
This American physicist won the 1989 Nobel for inventing the separated oscillatory field method behind atomic clocks, and helped found both Brookhaven National Laboratory and Fermilab — who was he?
Colloquially called harvestmen or daddy long legs, this arachnid order looks startlingly modern in 400-million-year-old fossils from Scotland's Rhynie cherts — what is it?
Opiliones: Order of arachnids. The Opiliones (formerly Phalangida) are an order of arachnids, colloquially known as harvestmen, harvesters, daddy long legs, or granddaddy long legs.

Sold over the counter under brand names like Tylenol and Panadol, this analgesic eases mild migraines and tension headaches but is famously inferior to ibuprofen at knocking down a fever — what is it?
Paracetamol: Medication for pain and fever.
This inflammation of the sac surrounding the heart causes sharp chest pain that eases when sitting up and worsens when lying down or breathing deeply — what condition is it?
Pericarditis: Inflammation of the pericardium. Pericarditis (PER-i-kar-DYE-tis) is inflammation of the pericardium, the fibrous sac surrounding the heart.
Their name blends the Greek for "plant" and "drifter": these self-feeding plankton photosynthesize in the sunlit surface waters of oceans and lakes — what are they?
Phytoplankton: Autotrophic members of the plankton ecosystem.
Named from the Latin word for 'bridge' after Italian anatomist Costanzo Varolio, this brainstem structure sits above the medulla and below the midbrain — what is it?
Pons: Part of the brainstem in humans and other bipeds.
Named after a Russian explorer and reintroduced to Mongolia's steppes after going extinct in the wild, this rare equine has 33 chromosome pairs instead of the usual 32 — what species is it?
Colorless and odorless, this radioactive noble gas with atomic number 86 is a decay product of radium and eventually settles into stable isotopes of lead?
Radon: Chemical element with atomic number 86 (Rn)
Made up of 12 paired bones plus the sternum and spine, this bony enclosure of the chest shields the heart and lungs while housing the muscles used for breathing — what is it?
Rib cage: Bone structure of the thorax.
Originally conceived as a jet trainer before its role expanded to supersonic strike and reconnaissance, this Anglo-French attack aircraft is today flown only by the Indian Air Force. What is it?
SEPECAT Jaguar: French/British attack aircraft. It was also later license produced by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited in India for use of the Indian Air Force.
Located at the base of the penis in most male mammals, this sac of skin holding the testicles tends to tighten when exposed to cold — what is it called?
Scrotum: Sac of skin that protects the testicles.
Named for a Swedish medical physicist, this SI unit measures the stochastic health risk of ionizing radiation, such as equivalent and effective dose — what unit is it?
Sievert: Derived SI unit of equivalent dose of ionizing radiation. One sievert equals 100 rem, which is an older, CGS radiation unit.
Also nicknamed 'sour dock,' this perennial herb native to Eurasia is often eaten as a tangy leaf vegetable in grassland habitats — which plant?
Sorrel: Flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae.
In this eye disorder, the two eyes fail to align properly on the same object, which can cause a lazy eye and lost depth perception if it persists through much of childhood. What condition is it?
Strabismus: Eyes not aligning when looking at something.
Named by Linnaeus in 1753 but called cempōhualxōchitl by the Nahua long before, this genus of Mexican-native flowers is commonly known as marigolds — what's the genus?

Taught in universities and seminaries, this academic discipline studies religious belief from within a religious perspective, focusing on divinity, revelation, and how God might interact with the world — what field is it?
Theology: Study of the nature of deities and religious beliefs.
